title: Data and its (dis)contents: A survey of dataset development and use in machine learning research

bias_targets.methodology: Literature review of dataset audits examining the under-representation of darker-skinned subjects in facial analysis datasets, as well as qualitative analyses exposing racial slurs and derogatory phrases used as labels in large-scale image datasets like ImageNet.

Literature review of studies identifying the under-representation of female pronouns, stereotype-aligned word co-occurrences in natural language processing datasets, and spurious correlations between gender and depicted activities in computer vision datasets.

Literature review of audits revealing disproportionate associations between queer identity terms and 'toxic' labels in NLP datasets, as well as critiques of pseudoscientific 'gaydar' datasets that rely on stereotypical grooming and self-expression cues.
Literature review of geographic representation studies demonstrating that images in standard object recognition datasets are overwhelmingly sourced from Western countries.
Literature review of studies finding that word co-occurrences in natural language processing datasets frequently reflect social biases and stereotypes related to (dis)ability.
